charge_energy_used_kwh.source: Energy that entered the car through its charge inlet during the session, as the car reports it, over the same span as `charge_energy_added_kwh`. AC session (`is_dc` false): the on-board charger's input energy, computed from the AC input power. It is what a meter before the car registers, apart from cable losses. Because it is computed from apparent power, it can overstate the real energy where the power factor is below 1 (about 1 % at 0.99, about 5 % at 0.95). DC session (`is_dc` true): the integral of the DC charging power the source reports. From sources with the Owner API's charge-state shape, on the one car measured so far, it was about 7 % above the battery-side counter (median of 81 sessions, never below), consistent with a reading taken before the battery. From Fleet Telemetry it is not yet measured. Unknown kind (`is_dc` null): the integral of the per-sample power the Hub selects. That is inlet energy for an AC session, and the reported DC power's integral for a DC session that showed no kind evidence. Null when not measured; no energy is invented for unobserved time. It prices no DC session (see `cost`).

charge_rate_km_per_hour.source: materialised charge projection; closed sessions only
charge_rate_km_per_hour.unit: km of range added per hour

cost.source: Cost of the session in currency units. Null means the cost is unknown: no complete tariff applied, its energy or time basis is missing, or nobody entered one. Zero is a known zero. Per-kWh tariffs: AC and unknown-kind sessions are priced on `charge_energy_used_kwh`, DC sessions on `charge_energy_added_kwh` only; a DC session without that figure has no per-kWh cost. Per-minute tariffs (`tariff_type` `per_minute`): the cost covers the whole connected time from `started_at_ms` to `ended_at_ms`, pauses included, in unrounded minutes. It is null when the stored samples show an unobserved stretch at either end of the session: the first sample is more than ten minutes after `started_at_ms`, the last two samples are more than ten minutes apart, or `ended_at_ms` is more than ten minutes after the last sample (the cases described under those keys). A session first seen in progress starts at its first sample and is priced over its observed time; a gap inside a session that later samples close is connected time and is priced; a row with no stored samples is priced over its own recorded start and end. Free Supercharging: when the owner's free-Supercharging setting is on, a session typed `Supercharger`, or a DC session of another DC type whose samples carry the charger brand Tesla and no other brand, costs zero. The session fee is added once per row (see `tariff_session_fee`). The Hub's automatic close and fill never overwrite a stored cost: a cost the import carried and a cost the owner entered stay. The owner can replace any stored cost, an imported one included. A total the owner enters replaces the cost and leaves the row's tariff unchanged. A unit price the owner enters, per kWh or per minute, replaces the row's tariff with that type and rate and no session fee, and the cost becomes the price on that tariff, with no free-charging rule and no fence fee; a per-minute price follows the per-minute rule above.
cost.unit: currency units; no currency code is carried; decimal serialised as a JSON number

ended_at_ms.source: End of the session. A session that continued across a period without data and then ended has as its end the first observation after that period, an upper bound: the true end lies between the last sample before the period and this time. A session recorded after a period without data (see `started_at_ms`) also ends at the first observation after it, an upper bound. For both, `duration_min` is an upper bound, and the stored samples show the period without data. A per-minute cost is computed only when the stored samples show no unobserved stretch at the start or the end of the session (see `cost`).

Later values do not change it. Values that say nothing (empty, `<invalid>`, `Unknown`, `SNA`, `Other`, `Tesla`) are skipped. A closed imported session whose import stored its type by an earlier rule keeps that value until it is imported again.

geofence_name.source: For a row the Hub collected: the name of the owner's geofence that contained the row's stored point when the row closed (the drive's start or end point; the charge's start point). Where fences overlap, the one with the smallest radius, then the nearest centre. Null when none did or the point is missing. For an imported row: the label the import source recorded. When the owner later creates, edits or deletes a geofence, stored rows are relabelled by one rule. A row whose point the change moves into or out of a fence takes the Hub's new answer there. A label that named a renamed fence takes the new name. Any other label, an imported one included, is kept, unless every fence of that name was deleted; then a row with a point takes the Hub's current answer there. Tariff fields and cost are never relabelled.

False when samples show AC evidence and none shows DC. Null when no sample says. started_at_ms.source: Start of the session. A session the Hub first saw already in progress starts at its first sample, which is then later than the true start (an upper bound); its added energy is still complete. A session the Hub records after a period without data, because the car's own energy counter shows energy was added while the Hub saw nothing, starts at the last time up to which the car's energy had been accounted for, which is earlier than the true start (a lower bound).

Currency units per kWh when `tariff_type` is `per_kwh`, per minute when `per_minute`. A unit price the owner enters replaces it.

tariff_session_fee.source: Session fee of the tariff recorded on the charge (see `tariff_type`). On a row the Hub collected that continues the previous row's plug-in (the car's own charging session continued with no unplug, drive or movement in between), the fee is waived so that a fee is charged once per connection: it is 0 when the tariff had a fee, and null, as in the tariff, when it had none. A unit price the owner enters replaces the tariff and clears the fee (null).
tariff_session_fee.unit: currency units; decimal serialised as a JSON number

tariff_type.source: The tariff recorded on the charge. For a charge the Hub collected: the tariff copied from the owner's geofence that contained its start point when it closed, or, when the owner asked the Hub to fill its missing cost after saving that geofence's tariff, the tariff of that geofence as the owner had just saved it. Later geofence edits never change it. It is null when no complete tariff was copied. For an imported charge: the tariff of the geofence the import source linked to the charge, as the import source held it when the history was imported; it is not a copy made when the session closed, and one of the three tariff keys can be null while another is not. For a charge whose price the owner entered as a unit price: the type the owner gave, which replaces any earlier tariff.

distance_km.source: Distance of the drive in km, from the odometer. When the Hub saw the car parked within its gap interval before the drive's first movement observation, the distance and the start values (start coordinates, battery level and ranges) are taken from that parked observation. They then include the stretch driven before the first movement observation, while `started_at_ms` and `duration_min` cover only the observed part. Distance divided by duration can therefore overstate the average speed by up to one parked polling interval of driving.

duration_min.source: Whole minutes of the observed drive, from `started_at_ms` to `ended_at_ms`. Saturated at 32767. When the drive starts from a recent parked observation, `distance_km` and the start values include the short stretch before the first movement observation, which this duration does not cover.

end_geofence_name.source: For a row the Hub collected: the name of the owner's geofence that contained the row's stored point when the row closed (the drive's start or end point; the charge's start point). Where fences overlap, the one with the smallest radius, then the nearest centre. Null when none did or the point is missing. For an imported row: the label the import source recorded. When the owner later creates, edits or deletes a geofence, stored rows are relabelled by one rule. A row whose point the change moves into or out of a fence takes the Hub's new answer there. A label that named a renamed fence takes the new name. Any other label, an imported one included, is kept, unless every fence of that name was deleted; then a row with a point takes the Hub's current answer there. Tariff fields and cost are never relabelled.

ended_at_ms.source: End of the drive. When the car did not state the end (for example a source that reports no gear, or a drive closed because evidence stopped arriving), the end is the Hub's last evidence that the drive was in progress: the first observation without movement evidence that follows the drive's last observation with movement evidence, or, if there is none, the last observation folded into the drive. An observation without movement evidence does not show that the car had stopped. Observations after that point are not counted in the drive's duration, distance or averages. The end is never earlier than `started_at_ms`.

null_rule: Null means unavailable, unknown, or not derivable. Preserve null and numeric zero distinctly; never infer a zero timestamp. Current owner/stream merge ignores null overlays. No freshness guarantee beyond observed_at_ms. Optional provenance fields may be absent or null; absent and null mean no truthful record exists.
number_rule: position.power and the charge_sample fields charger_power_kw, charger_voltage, charger_actual_current and charger_pilot_current are whole numbers in the source database but are typed number, because the page routes serve the materialised projections of the Hub, which hold them as floating point: a whole value may carry a fraction digit (12 or 12.0). Clients accept both. Retyping these fields later is a new major profile.
